case.role: First-year article assistant on the direct-tax team’s TDS desk
case.client: Tamhini Drivetech Private Limited, a Chakan company that makes gears, shafts and hubs for vehicle makers, with a depot at Hosur in Tamil Nadu; it also trades aftermarket parts
case.team: Kunal Mehrotra (tax senior); Pallavi Shinde (accounts executive at Tamhini, keeps the TDS working)
case.goal: Check ten payments before Tamhini’s October–December TDS statement is filed, tie TDS receivable to Form 168 and build the statement summary.
case.where: Accounts room, Chakan plant · Monday 18 January 2027

messages: Tamhini’s October–December TDS statement is due on 31 January. I’ve pulled ten payments from Pallavi’s working: check section and rate on each, and mark what’s short.
Then tie their TDS receivable to Form 168 and build the summary. By Thursday the 28th, please; I want to file on Friday the 29th.

documents.subtitle: Bapat Venkatesh & Co. · direct-tax desk · Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) Table

rows.p: Rent or hire of plant, machinery or equipment
Rent of land, building, furniture or fittings

rows.w: is over ₹30,000 on a bill, or ₹1,00,000 in the year

rows.p: Contract work: firm, LLP, company or any other
rows.w: is over ₹30,000 on a bill, or ₹1,00,000 in the year
crosses ₹50 lakh in the year: only on the part above

notes: A year’s limit, once crossed, brings in the whole year’s amount, earlier bills included. The ₹30,000 bill limit and the monthly rent limit bring in only that bill or that month. Purchase of goods is the exception: only the part above ₹50 lakh.
Deduct when the bill is credited or paid, whichever comes first.
When that date falls on or after 1 April 2026, quote the section 393 entry and code, not the old 194C, 194H, 194-I, 194J or 194Q.

Contract work is any work done under a contract, supply of labour included: job work on the client’s parts, carriage of goods, catering, and making a product to the client’s specification from material bought from the client. From tax year 2026–27 it also includes supply of manpower to work under the client’s supervision. A product made to the client’s specification from the supplier’s own material is a purchase.
Professional services: legal, medical, engineering, architecture, accountancy, technical consultancy, interior decoration, advertising and notified professions.
No TDS for a transporter who owns ten or fewer goods carriages and gives a declaration with PAN: report the payment with code T.
On services, deduct on the amount before GST when the bill shows GST separately.
For Tamhini: a company with turnover over ₹10 crore last year, so every row above applies to it.

tasks.title: Check section and rate on ten payments
tasks.prompt: Open each payment with its bills and ledger; the rate card, the vendor master and Pallavi’s working are under Other papers. Decide which section 393 entry it falls under, the rate it needs, and whether what was deducted for October–December is fine or short.

lockOnLeave.ask: Hand your ten payment calls to Kunal?
lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change them after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Kunal. You can read your calls but not change them.

hints: Decide what was paid for from the bill and the contract, not from the ledger it was booked in. Then who is paid: an individual, a firm or a company.
Check the limit: one bill, one month or the year’s total, earlier bills included. Then look for a paper that switches TDS off.

fields.label: Rate to deduct on these payments
Your note for the file
fields.placeholder: For example: bill of 30 Nov, firm, 2% on ₹1,20,000

items.label: Payment 1 · Jadhavwadi Manpower Services
items.prompt: Contract labour at the Chakan plant, a bill a month.
items.note: Payment 1: Fine. Supplying manpower to work under Tamhini’s supervisors is “work” in so many words from this year, so it is contract work. Jadhavwadi is a firm: 2% on ₹66,99,900 is ₹1,33,998, as deducted.

items.label: Payment 2 · Sakhare Surface Treatment
items.prompt: Phosphating and blackening on Tamhini’s shafts and flanges.
items.note: Payment 2: Fine. Sakhare Surface Treatment is Mangesh Sakhare’s proprietorship, so the contractor is an individual: 1%. Job work on Tamhini’s own parts is contract work, not a purchase. ₹29,306 is right.

items.label: Payment 3 · Kudalwadi Heat Treaters
items.prompt: Heat treatment of Tamhini’s gears and shafts.
items.note: Payment 3: Short. Kudalwadi is a partnership firm, so 2%, not 1%: ₹1,08,852 for the quarter against ₹54,426 deducted. Short ₹54,426. April to September carry the same 1%, so those quarters need correcting too.

items.label: Payment 4 · Senthil Kumaran
items.prompt: Rent for the Hosur depot’s warehouse.
items.note: Payment 4: Fine. A warehouse is a building: 10% on ₹2,50,000 a month, far over the ₹50,000 a month limit. ₹75,000 for the quarter, worked on the rent before GST.

items.label: Payment 5 · Ambethan Power Rentals
items.prompt: A DG set on monthly hire from October.
items.note: Payment 5: Short. A DG set hired without an operator is rent of machinery: 2% on ₹85,000 a month, ₹5,100 for the quarter, and nothing deducted. Booked under Power and fuel, it never reached Pallavi’s draft statement.

items.label: Payment 6 · Adv. Medha Paranjpe
items.prompt: Legal fees on the distributor agreement.
items.note: Payment 6: Short. Her August bill of ₹35,000 was under the limit on its own. December’s ₹60,000 takes the year to ₹95,000, so 10% is due on all of it: ₹9,500. ₹6,000 deducted, ₹3,500 short.

items.label: Payment 7 · Rupesh Dhakne
items.prompt: Tamhini’s new agent for aftermarket orders in Marathwada.
items.note: Payment 7: Short. Each bill is under ₹20,000, but the year’s commission is ₹32,500. Once the total crosses the limit, 2% is due on the whole ₹32,500: ₹650. Booked under Sales promotion, so nobody looked.

items.label: Payment 8 · Mahalunge Roadlines
items.note: Payment 8: Fine. Mahalunge owns 26 trucks and gave no declaration, so the small-transporter exemption is out either way. Carrying goods is contract work and Mahalunge is a firm, so 2%: ₹99,634 is right.

items.label: Payment 9 · Dnyaneshwar Kalbhor
items.prompt: Truck trips from Chakan to the Hosur depot.
items.note: Payment 9: Fine. Kalbhor owns two trucks and signed a declaration with his PAN before his first trip. No TDS on his bills, but he still goes in the statement, with code T.

items.label: Payment 10 · Kolak Polypack
items.prompt: Printed VCI bags and stretch film.
items.note: Payment 10: Fine. Bags made to Tamhini’s drawing from Kolak’s own film are a purchase, not contract work. Purchases this year are ₹34,27,000, under ₹50 lakh, so nothing is due yet. Keep an eye on it till March.

tasks.title: Before the statement goes
tasks.prompt: Three things Kunal will ask before he files on Friday: December’s challans, your short deductions and the dates.
hints: Two different dates are at work here: when the tax had to reach the bank, and when the statement has to reach the department.

questions.text: December’s two challans went in on 11 January. What does that mean for this statement?

options.text: They were late, so a fee of ₹200 a day runs from 7 January until the statement is filed.
options.why: That fee is for filing the statement late, not for depositing late. A late deposit costs interest.

options.text: They were late: interest at 1.5% a month or part, from deduction to deposit, is paid before filing.
options.why: Due by 7 January. The challans carry ₹6,919 of interest; check it against the deduction dates before Friday.

options.text: They were on time: a month’s TDS can go in until the 15th of the next month, so nothing more is due.
options.why: The 7th, except March, which has till 30 April. 11 January is four days late.

options.text: They were late, so 30% of December’s contract and fee bills cannot be claimed as expenses in this tax year.
options.why: Not when the TDS is paid long before the return is due on 31 October 2027. The cost here is interest.

questions.text: Your short deductions add up to the fresh challan in your summary. What happens to them before Friday?

options.text: We file as drafted, and Tamhini pays the shorts when the department’s notice of the default lists them.
options.why: Filing a statement you know is short invites a default notice and more interest. Fix it before it goes.

options.text: Tamhini recovers them from the same vendors’ next bills and shows them in the January–March statement.
options.why: Recovering from the next bills is fine between Tamhini and the vendors. The tax itself is due now, in this quarter.

options.text: Tamhini deposits them now on a fresh challan with interest, so each payee’s row shows the full TDS.
options.why: Interest on a short deduction is paid before the statement goes. Then every payee’s row is right, and so is their credit.

options.text: Nothing now: the tax audit will report them, and 30% of those bills is disallowed in the return.
options.why: Left alone, the bills with nothing deducted lose 30% in the return, and the tax audit reports every short either way. Deduct and pay the TDS this year, and nothing is disallowed.

questions.text: By when must this statement be filed, and the certificates in Form 131 (Form 16A until March 2026) issued?

options.text: By 31 January 2027; the certificates in Form 131 by 15 June 2027, after the year ends.
options.why: 15 June is for salary certificates, in Form 130. Other payments get Form 131 within fifteen days of the statement’s due date.

options.text: By 15 February 2027; the certificates in Form 131 go out with the statement itself.
options.why: The statement is due on 31 January. 15 February is the certificates’ date.

options.text: By 7 February 2027, with January’s challan; the certificates in Form 131 within a month of filing.
options.why: 7 February is when January’s tax must be deposited. The statement is due on 31 January.

options.text: By 31 January 2027; the certificates in Form 131 within fifteen days after, by 15 February 2027.
options.why: Statements for October–December are due by 31 January. The fifteen days for certificates other than salary count from that due date, not from the day the statement is filed.

wrap.text: Four shorts, ₹63,676, each with its own cause: a firm taken for an individual, hire booked as power, commission booked as promotion, a limit read bill by bill. Pallavi deposits it with interest this week and I file on Friday the 29th. Vaigai’s correction and Tamhini’s two entries are yours to chase.

wrapPartial.text: Four of the ten were short, ₹63,676, and two of them hid under the wrong ledger head: hire as power, commission as promotion. The challan and Tamhini’s entries come from your figures, so the summary and the six deductors have to be right before Pallavi deposits or posts anything.

wrapRetry.text: Section follows what a payment is, not the ledger it was booked in; then the payee, then the limit. For Form 168, find whose paper is wrong, quarter by quarter. Build the summary from Pallavi’s draft plus your shorts.

passNeeds.note: You need more of the ten payment calls right to pass.
Tie more of the six deductors to Form 168 before this passes.
The statement summary needs more figures right, or following your figures, before this passes.

model.intro: Four payments were short by ₹63,676 in all; the other six were right, two of them with nothing to deduct. Of the six deductors, two match, two need Tamhini’s books corrected, one must correct its own statement, and one is timing.

rows.a: Ask Vaigai to correct Tamhini’s PAN in its July–September statement
Book the TDS and gross up September’s interest to ₹1,01,250
Correct the August entry from 9,809 to 9,089

blocks.text: Before Friday: ₹63,676 goes on a fresh challan with interest, and the four payees’ rows show the full TDS. December’s challans were four days late, and their ₹6,919 of interest went with them. Kudalwadi’s April–September short is deposited too, with interest, and those quarters get correction statements.

Two of the three new payees in your ten, Ambethan and Rupesh, never reached the draft. Start each quarter with the vendor master’s new names, and test the old rates too: Kudalwadi’s 1% has run since April.

principles: Classify the payment from the bill and the contract, then the payee, then the limit: one bill, one month or the year’s total.
Credit follows Form 168, so find whose paper is wrong: the deductor corrects its statement, the client corrects its books, or it is timing.
Interest on a short deduction or a late deposit is paid before the statement goes, not after a notice.

interview.q: What do you check before you deduct TDS on a payment?
interview.checking: Whether you start from what the payment is, not from habit or the ledger it was booked in.
outline: What the payment is, from the bill and the contract, not the ledger head; then who is paid.
Then the limit: one bill, one month or the year’s total; then the rate, contractors 1% or 2%.
In the simulation I classified payments to {payees} vendors that way[[ and found {short} short {short|deduction|deductions}]].

interview.q: A client’s books and the tax-credit statement show different TDS. What do you do?
interview.checking: Whether you explain each difference instead of forcing it, and know that credit follows Form 168.
outline: Credit follows Form 168, so I match it deductor by deductor and quarter by quarter.
A wrong PAN or a missing statement is the deductor’s to fix; I check their certificate first.
A missed or wrong entry in the books is corrected there; a later entry is only timing.
